violations.text: The non-food contact surfaces of the crushed ice machine have an accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned to sight and touch. New Violation. Correct By: 06/01/2026

Food contact surfaces of equipment/utensils ice machine were observed with an accumulation of food and debris. The food contact surfaces of equipment must be clean to sight and touch. Ice machine was turned off and emptied at the time of inspection. Establishment is not to use ice machine until it is properly cleaned and sanitized. New Violation. Correct By: 05/21/2026

Puree, which was previously cooked and cooled, was not reheated for hot holding. Time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food that is cooked, cooled, and reheated for hot holding must be reheated to 165 degrees Fahrenheit or above for 15 seconds. Puree was reheated to above 165 DF at the time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 05/21/2026

Various food was observed held between 52-54 degrees Fahrenheit in the walk-in cooler. Time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food must be held at 41 degrees Fahrenheit or below except during preparation, cooking, or cooling. Establishment had a food delivery 4 hours prior to inspection. All food that was delivered today was moved to properly functioning refrigeration. All food in unit was evaluated and either voluntarily disposed of or moved at the time of inspection. Establishment is not to store any TCS foods in walk-in cooler until it is able to hold an ambient temperature of 41 DF or less. Service was called at the time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 05/21/2026

Proper cooling methods were not used for time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods. Per interview of PIC, sauce was placed hot in the refrigerator in containers greater than four inches deep. Sauce was placed into ice bath at the time of inspections. Proper cooling methods reviewed with PIC. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 05/21/2026

Beef was observed thawing in stagnant water at the time of inspection. Time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods must be thawed in one of the following manners: under refrigeration (41 degrees Fahrenheit or less); completely submerged under running water; as part of the cooking process; or in the microwave if cooked immediately after thawing. Beef was completely submerged under running water at the time of inspection. Proper thawing methods reviewed. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 05/21/2026
The walk-in cooler was observed holding an ambient of 54 DF and in poor repair. Equipment must be maintained in good repair. New Violation. Correct By: 05/21/2026
The handwashing sink at the dining room bar was non-functional at the time of inspection, with the faucet disconnected. PIC called for service. New Violation. Correct By: 01/16/2026

The chlorine sanitizer concentration for the sanitizing cycle of the kitchen and rear bar dishwashers was under 25 parts per million (ppm). Chlorine sanitizing solutions must be between 50-100 ppm. PIC scheduled service. New Violation. Correct By: 01/16/2026

Food contact surfaces of equipment/utensils (ice machine) were observed with an accumulation of food and debris. The food contact surfaces of equipment must be clean to sight and touch. New Violation. Correct By: 01/22/2026

Utensils in the utensil crock are displayed with the lip surface up. Utensils are to be stored so that only the handles are touched by employees and consumers if consumer self-service is provided. New Violation. Correct By: 01/15/2026
A leak was observed at the drain of the handwashing sink at the dining room bar. New Violation. Correct By: 01/29/2026
The corner wall of the dining room bar was unsealed/unfinished. PIC stated wall is scheduled for repair. New Violation. Correct By: 01/29/2026
